pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: The migration 0002_add_priority.sql has a CHECK constraint and DEFAULT 'normal'. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks all 3 rows are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected. The spec text was weakened from 'every' to 'most' by the last commit (see finding). The code and test still deliver 'every'.
test 'AC-2' asserts the exact <li> text for high, low and normal items.
test 'AC-3' covers high, low and normal filters, with ordering checked for high (ids 1,3).
test 'AC-4' checks all items in id order with no filter.
test 'AC-5' asserts the full nav HTML for all four views, with the current filter as <strong>.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty and __proto__. The handler uses searchParams.has plus a Set.
test 'AC-7' checks the high, low and normal messages, and 'No items yet.' in all four views after DELETE.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'. test 'AC-8' asserts it. The fake app in test/traffic.test.js now records the query string, and scripts/traffic-config-check.mjs accepts queries.

findings.what: The last commit, 'Follow-up edits' by github-actions[bot], changes AC-1 from 'every existing item gets normal' to 'most existing item gets normal'. This edits an acceptance item after the go (2026-10-12) with no decision in the spec recording the owner's call and date. It weakens the requirement, and the wording is also ungrammatical.
findings.fix: Revert AC-1 to 'every existing item gets normal'. If the owner really wants the change, record it as a dated decision.

findings.what: The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing', but the final commit rewrites AC-1 after the go.
findings.fix: Revert the edit, or list the AC-1 change under 'Changed after the go' with the owner's decision.

findings.what: AC-8 only checks that routes.json contains the string. It does not show that the traffic Worker requests the query path; the fake app change in test/traffic.test.js has no test using a query route.
findings.fix: Add a traffic test that fetches the routes, including the query route, and asserts the query reaches the app.

lenses.note: A spec exists and is followed. The one departure is the post-go edit to AC-1.
All 8 items are implemented and each is named by a test. The 4 state rows have tests. AC-1 was reworded after the go.
The tests assert real output. I did not run them (the Cloudflare workers test environment may not be installed here; CI runs them). AC-8 is weakly evidenced.
The README mentions the filter. The README's traffic description is unchanged and still accurate.
No defects found. Validation is strict, the SQL is parameterised, and the extra COUNT query is only used to tell 'no match' from an empty table.
The query value is validated against a fixed Set before use and titles are escaped. No injection found.
Only a minimal server-rendered nav, with no stylesheet or component changes. No visual design review is applicable beyond the spec'd markup.
No browser session is available and the PR gives no preview. The behaviour is covered by Worker-level tests.
The 'Changed after the go: nothing' claim is false, because AC-1 was edited by the last commit.
